text: ভূগোল, পরিবেশ ও দুযোর্গ ব্যবস্থাপনা বাংলাদেশের সাথে দুটি দেশের সীমানা রয়েছে। যথা- ভারত এবং মিয়ানমার। সীমান্তবতীর্ রাজ্য ও জেলা- ভারত বাংলাদেশের সাথে ভারতের সীমানা রয়েছে— ৫টি রাজ্যের। যথা— আসাম, মিজোরাম, ত্রিপুরা, মেঘালয়, পশ্চিমবঙ্গ। (মনে রাখার উপায়: আমি মেঘে ত্রিপুরা পাই)। বাংলাদেশের সীমান্তবতীর্ ভারতের সেভেন সিস্টাসর্ রাজ্য— ৪টি (আসাম, মিজোরাম, মেঘালয় ও ত্রিপুরা)। বাংলাদেশের সীমান্তবতীর্ নয় এমন সেভেন সিস্টাসর্ রাজ্য— ৩টি (মণিপুর, নাগাল্যান্ড ও অরুণাচল)। ভারতের সাথে বাংলাদেশের সীমান্তবতীর্ জেলা— ৩০ টি। বাংলাদেশের সীমান্তবতীর্ ভারতের পশ্চিমবঙ্গের জেলা— ৯টি। যথা— মালদহ, মুশির্দাবাদ, নদীয়া, উত্তর চব্বিশ পরগনা, উত্তর দিনাজপুর, দক্ষিণ দিনাজপুর, জলপাইগুড়ি, কুচবিহার, দাজিির্লং। মিয়ানমার বাংলাদেশের সাথে মিয়ানমারের সীমান্তবতীর্ রাজ্য— ২টি (রাখাইন ও শান)। মিয়ানমারের সাথে বাংলাদেশের সীমান্তবতীর্ জেলা— ৩টি (রাঙামাটি, বান্দরবান, কক্সবাজার)। বাংলাদেশ-ভারত অমীমাংসিত সীমান্ত— ২.৫ কিলোমিটার (মহুরীর চর)।

text: পৃথিবীর বায়ুম-ল এবং বহিঃমহাকাশের (Outer Space) মধ্যবতীর্ সীমানা নিধার্রণকারী কাল্পনিক রেখাটিকে কারমান লাইন বলা হয়। এটি সমুদ্রপৃষ্ঠ থেকে সাধারণত ১০০ কিলোমিটার (প্রায় ৬২ মাইল) উচ্চতায় অবস্থিত। হাঙ্গেরীয়-মাকির্ন প্রকৌশলী এবং পদাথির্বদ থিওডোর ফন কারমান-এর নামানুসারে এর নামকরণ করা হয়েছে। তিনি প্রথম হিসাব করে দেখিয়েছিলেন যে, এই উচ্চতায় বায়ুম-ল এতটাই পাতলা হয়ে যায় যে সাধারণ উড়োজাহাজ আর উড়তে পারে না; সেখানে ওড়ার জন্য মহাকাশযানের গতি প্রয়োজন। বিভিন্ন ধরনের কাল্পনিক রেখা- কাল্পনিক রেখা যে যে সমবিন্দুকে সংযুক্ত করে কাল্পনিক রেখা যে যে সমবিন্দুকে সংযুক্ত করে আইসোহাইট সমবষর্ণ রেখা আইসোপিল্লথ কোন উৎপন্ন দ্রব্য বা ঘটনার সমপরিমাণ রেখা আইসোহ্যালাইন সামুদ্রিক সমলবণতা রেখা আইসোথামর্ সম উষ্ণতা রেখা আইসোবার সমবায়ুম-লীয় চাপসম্পন্ন স্থানসমূহ দ্বিতীয় অধ্যায়: অঞ্চলভিত্তিক ভৌত পরিবেশ (ভূ-প্রাকৃতিক), সম্পদের বণ্টন ও গুরুত্ব.

text: ১ নটিক্যাল মাইল = ৬০৮০ ফুট। ভূ-ত্বকের অভ্যন্তরীণ গঠন উপাদান সাধারণত স্থলপথে ব্যবহৃত মাইলের (Statute Mile) তুলনায় নটিক্যাল মাইল কিছুটা বড় হয়। সমুদ্রপথে বা আকাশপথে দূরত্ব পরিমাপের জন্য এই এককটি আন্তজাির্তকভাবে ব্যবহৃত হয়। ১ নটিক্যাল মাইল ≈ ১.১৫১ মাইল (স্থলপথের মাইল)। ১ নটিক্যাল মাইল ≈ ১.৮৫২ কিলোমিটার। পৃথিবীর বাহ্যিক গঠন.

text: দ্বীপ অবস্থান আয়তন অপর নাম গুরুত্বপূর্ণ তথ্য সেন্টমাটির্ন টেকনাফ, কক্সবাজার (বঙ্গোপসাগরে) ৮ বর্গ কি.মি. নারিকেল জিঞ্জিরা  দেশের একমাত্র সামুদ্রিক প্রবাল দ্বীপ।  খনিজ পদাথর্ (চুনাপাথর, কালো সোনা প্রভৃতি) পাওয়া যায়। ছেঁড়া দ্বীপ টেকনাফ, কক্সবাজার (বঙ্গোপসাগরে অবস্থিত) ৩ বর্গ কি.মি. -  বাংলাদেশের সবর্দক্ষিণের স্থান।  সেন্টমাটিের্নর দক্ষিণে অবস্থিত। ভোলা ভোলা (মেঘনা নদীর মোহনায়) ১৪৪১ বর্গ কি.মি. দক্ষিণ শাহবাজপুর  দেশের একমাত্র দ্বীপ জেলা।  দেশের বৃহত্তম দ্বীপ। মনপুরা ভোলা ৩৭৩ বর্গ কি.মি. -  মেঘনা নদীর মোহনায় অবস্থিত।  এই দ্বীপে পতুর্গীজরা বসবাস করত। শাহপরীর দ্বীপ টেকনাফ, কক্সবাজার ৫ বর্গ কি.মি. শাপরী/শাহপুরা  নাফ নদীর মোহনায় বাংলাদেশ- মিয়ানমার সীমান্তে অবস্থিত। সন্দ্বীপ চট্টগ্রাম ৫ বর্গ কি.মি. -  দেশের সবচেয়ে প্রাচীন জনবসতিপূর্ণ দ্বীপ। বাংলাদেশের পযর্টন শিল্প.

text: ঘূর্ণিঝড় 'সিডর' (Sidr)  একটি অত্যন্ত শক্তিশালী ট্রপিক্যাল সাইক্লোন যা ১৫ নভেম্বর ২০০৭ সালে বাংলাদেশের উপকূলে (বিশেষ করে দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিমাঞ্চলে) আঘাত হানে। এর ফলে প্রচুর জীবনহানি ও সুন্দরবনের ব্যাপক ক্ষতি হয়েছিল। ঘূর্ণিঝড় 'আইলা' (Aila), সিডরের প্রায় দুই বছর পর ২৫ মে ২০০৯ সালে বাংলাদেশের দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিম উপকূলীয় জেলাগুলোতে আঘাত হানে। এটি দীর্ঘস্থায়ী জলোচ্ছ্বাসের জন্য পরিচিত ছিল যা উপকূলীয় বাঁধ ভেঙে লবণাক্ত পানি লোকালয়ে ঢুকিয়ে দিয়েছিল। ঘূর্ণিঝড় রিমাল (Remal) আঘাত হাতে ২০২৪ সালে।

text: দুযোর্গ ব্যবস্থাপনার পযার্য়ক্রম পূবর্ প্রস্তুতি > ঝুঁকি চিহ্নিতকরণ > পুনবার্সন > প্রতিরোধ > প্রশমন। দুযোর্গ প্রতিরোধ, দুযোর্গ প্রশমন এবং দুযোের্গর পূবর্প্রস্তুতি দুযোর্গ ব্যবস্থাপনার মুখ্য উপাদান। সুতরাং দুযোর্গকে কাযর্ত মোকাবিলার লক্ষ্যে দুযোর্গপূবর্ সময়েই এর ব্যবস্থাপনার বেশি কাজ সম্পন্ন করতে হয়। দুর্যোগ সংঘটনের পরপরই এর ব্যবস্থাপনা সম্পূর্ণ ব্যবস্থাপনার অন্যান্য উপাদানের মধ্যে রয়েছে সাড়াদান, পুনরুদ্ধার ও উন্নয়ন। অতীতে সাড়াদানকেই সম্পূর্ণ দুর্যোগ ব্যবস্থাপনা বলে ধরে নেওয়া হতো। প্রস্তুতি (Preparedness): দুযোর্গ আসার আগেই জনগণকে সচেতন করা, আশ্রয়কেন্দ্র ঠিক করা এবং পরিকল্পনা করা। (এটিই প্রথম ধাপ) সাড়া প্রদান (Response): দুযোর্গ চলাকালীন উদ্ধারকাজ ও জরুরি সহায়তা। পুনরুদ্ধার ও পুনবার্সন (Recovery & Rehabilitation): দুযোের্গর পর ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত্মদের সহায়তা ও ঘরবাড়ি মেরামত। প্রশমন (Mitigation): ভবিষ্যতের দুযোের্গর ঝুঁকি কমানোর জন্য স্থায়ী ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ। মুখ্য উপাদান গৌণ উপাদান

txt: সারাংশ লিখুন: "প্রকৃত জ্ঞানের স্পৃহা না থাকলে শিক্ষা ব্যর্থতায় পর্যবসিত হয়। তখন পরীক্ষায় পাসটাই বড় হয় এবং পাঠ্যপুস্তকের পৃষ্ঠায় জ্ঞান সীমাবদ্ধ থাকে। এই কারণেই পরীক্ষায় পাস করা লোকের অভাব নেই আমাদের দেশে, কিন্তু অভাব আছে জ্ঞানীর। যেখানেই পরীক্ষা-পাসের মোহ তরুণ ছাত্রছাত্রীদের উৎকণ্ঠিত রাখে, সেখানেই জ্ঞান নির্বাসিত জীবনযাপন করে। একটি স্বাধীন জাতি হিসেবে জগতের বুকে অক্ষয় আসন লাভ করতে হলে জ্ঞানের প্রতি তরুণসমাজকে অনুপ্রাণিত করতে হবে। সহজ লাভ আপাতত সুখের হলেও পরিণামে কল্যাণ বহন করে না। পরীক্ষা পাসের মোহ থেকে মুক্ত না হলে তরুণ সমাজের সামনে কখনোই জ্ঞানের দিগন্ত উন্মোচিত হবে না।"

04. Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
When we look up at the night sky, we can see both stars and planets in a single gaze. But do we know that though they look similar, they differ from one another in many ways? In fact, most of the glittering dots in the sky are huge balls of fire like our sun. But we do not feel their heat because they are trillions of miles away from us. Unlike the stars, planets are balls of cold gas or solid rocks and they revolve around their respective stars. Earth and its neighbouring Mars are planets that move around the sun. Stars are of different sizes and colours. The newly born stars are bluish white. When stars come near the end of their life, they become white, small and dense. These stars are called 'White Dwarfs'. Huge stars that have burned most of their fuel turn red and are called 'Red Giants'. Like stars, planets also vary in colour and size. Our planet is like a small ball compared to Jupiter, which is a huge ball of gas and is called a 'Gas Giant'. Saturn is another Gas Giant in our solar system which has a beautiful set of rings. The earth looks blue, the Mars is red, while the Jupiter is Orange.
Questions:
a) Give a suitable title of the passage.
b) What are the differences between a star and a planet?
c) Make a new sentence using the words 'compared to'.
d) What is the meaning of the word 'glittering'?
e) Summarize the passage in your own words.

12. Read the passage carefully and answer the following question:
One of the greatest advance in modern technology is the invention of computers. They are already used in industries and in universities and time may come when it will be possible for ordinary people to use them as well. As computers are capable of doing extremely complicated work in all branches of learning, they can solve the most complex mathematical problems or put thousands of unrelated facts in order. These machines can be put to various uses. For instance, they can provide information on the best way to prevent traffic accident or they can count the number. They work accurately and at high speeds, they save research worker's years of hard work. This whole process by which machines can be used to work for us has been called automation. In the future, automation may enable humans to enjoy for more leisure than they do today. The coming of automation is found to have important social consequences.
Questions:
a) Which is considered to be the greatest invention of modern technology?
b) What are the uses that computers are put to?
c) What are computers capable of doing?
d) What is automation and how can it help man in future?
e) How do computers save researcher's years of hard work?

Education in state schools in Britain is free and compulsory for everybody from the age of five to the age of sixteen. It is free for the next two years also. Having taken the general certificate of Education at ordinary level in five or six subjects at the age of sixteen, a student who wishes to go to the university must take two or three subjects at advanced level. If he will probably take English, French and German of perhaps Spanish. If he wants to study medicine, he will take biology, physics and chemistry or perhaps botany and zoology. During these two years after O'Level he will study intensively and in greater depth than his education so far. At eighteen, he must apply for admission and to be safe, generally apply to three or four universities putting them in an order of preference. His application is made through the University Central Council on Admission (UCCA) who then start the admission process.

Questions:
a) Upto what age does a British student get free education?
b) What are the criteria for qualifying for the university admission?

ইংরেজি Reading Comprehension

Read the following passage and answer the questions given below:
"No one knows who discovered that the silkworm could be used to clothe people. At first the making of silk was kept a great secret. The kings of China warned their people not to teach strangers the way it was done. They even gave orders that no silk worm eggs were to be allowed out of the country, and that anyone breaking the rules be severely punished.
Silk is a textile that is useful as well as beautiful. It comes from the cocoon of the silkworm. There are four stages in the life of the silkworm. First, there is an egg. The egg hatches and a kind of caterpillar known as a silkworm comes out. It eats, grows and bursts out of its skin several times. It then spins a long, slender thread and winds the thread round and round its body. It goes to sleep in this silken nest or cocoon. The silkworm is now a chrysalis. Inside the cocoon, chrysalis changes into butterfly. It then breaks out of the cocoon for the last stage of its life, as an insect. But many millions of silkworms do not live to become butterflies. To get the silk, the silkworkers kill the chrysalises inside the cocoons by the use of hot steam."

a) How many stages are there in the life of silkworms?
b) Where does the silkworm go to sleep?
c) When does the silkworm change from a chrysalis to a butterfly?
d) What is a cocoon made of?
e) Why do silkworkers kill the chrysalises?

Read the passage and then answer the questions that follow:
"Self-reliance is the pilgrim's best staff, the worker's best tool. It is the master key that unlocks all the difficulties of life. 'Help yourself and Heaven will help you' is a maxim which receives daily confirmation. Help from within always strengthens; but help from without invariably weakens the recipient. The habit of depending on others tends to weaken the intellectual faculties and paralyse the judgment. The struggle against adverse circumstances has, on the contrary, a strengthening effect, like of the pure mountain air on any enfeebled frame. This is a lesson which is not taught in schools nowadays. The vice of the modern system of education is that it lays down too many royal roads to knowledge. The difficulties which formerly compelled a student to think and labour for himself are now most carefully removed. The race of thorough and complete scholars is dying out. Our young men are equipped to such an extent with manuals that explain everything and guides that go everywhere, that they find no occasion for thought. Why do you take any trouble at all when so many are willing to relieve you of it?"

a) What, according to the writer, is the bad side of modern system of education?
b) Why should students be self-reliant?

"Self control is at the root of many human virtues. Let a man give the rein to his impulses and passions for his moral freedom. Failure to achieve this freedom may lead one to slavery and degradation. He is carried along with the current of life and thus becomes a slave of his own strongest desires for the time being. To be morally free, to be more than an animal- a man must be able to resist instinctive impulse and this can only be done by the exercise and practice of self-control. This is the power which constitutes the real distinction between physical and moral life, and forms the primary basis of individual character. Praise is given not to the strong man who 'taketh the city' but to the stronger man who 'rules his own spirit'. Really strong is he who, by discipline exercises a constant control over his emotions, his speeches, and his acts. Ninety percent of vicious desires that degrade society are direct outgrowth from the lack of self-discipline, self-respect and self-control."

"পুণ্যে পাপে দুঃখে সুখে পতনে উত্থানে
মানুষ হইতে দাও তোমার সন্তানে

প্রাণ দিয়ে দুঃখ স'য়ে আপনার হাতে

Read the passage below and answer the questions:
"Mushroom, the fungi food, is a small wonder of nature. But we have been neglecting that vegetable for so long. One of the reasons is the misconception that it grows in filthy and soggy places and has something to do with frogs. Besides all of us are not well aware of the nutritional qualities and medicinal values. From controlling blood pressure to helping take care of an ailing stomach, mushrooms have wide range of beneficial roles. Believe it or not, this vegetable has low fat, good protein and vitamins that can help reduce stress, fat mass around your waist. Moreover, it provides preventive against jaundice, premature hair loss and anemia. So cultivation of mushroom will provide job creation for the unemployed youths along with opening a new horizon for exports earning for Bangladesh. Considering mushroom as a potential source for medicinal substitutes as well as economical and financial viables, public and private financial institutions should come forward to encourage farmers to grow mushroom by lending money on easy terms."

Questions:
(a) What is the main reason for neglecting the vegetable mushroom for so long?
(b) What are the medicinal values of mushroom?
(c) What are the financial viabilities of mushroom?
(d) How farmers can be motivated to cultivate mushroom?
(e) How the public and private sector involve in mushroom production?

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the questions below it:
"Feeding the ever-growing population is a big challenge for Bangladesh in the coming decade. The major challenge for the country is to sustain the current level of agricultural production. The task is daunting, especially when the country loses about 80 thousand hectares of cultivable land annually due to excessive pressure on land for human settlement as well as the building of infrastructure such as roads and bridges. Moreover, river erosion and other non-agricultural uses contribute to the diminishing of agricultural land. Although the total numbers of farm holding have increased by 18 percent, the cultivated area has declined with the average farm size decreasing form 2.26 acres in 1983-1984 to 1.69 in 1996. Given that, about 80% of the farms are small and highly fragmented, more imaginative and effective organizations of production are needed to sustain agricultural productivity and create more employment and income for the farming community. The newly emerging contract farming taken up by a number of private agribusiness firms is one of the approach to promoting food production, especially fruit and vegetables. One possibility to compensate for the loss of land is to go for land reclamation in the Bay of Bengal for which, of course, the country needs massive external assistance. It is essential to improve agricultural production in general and food production in particular, For this, support from the public sector is necessary to generate and promote technologies and hence to strengthen production. Biotechnology research and development of hybrid crops and animal species need to be given priority which will probably involve partnership with multinational private sector firms and institutions."

Questions:
(a) What are the two challenges for Bangladesh in the coming decade?
(b) What possible thing can be done to compensate for the loss of land?
(c) Why does the country lose cultivable land every year?
(d) How has the cultivable area declined?
(e) How would you describe our farmers?

txt:
Read the passage below and answer the following questions:
"It has been over three hundred years since emperor Shahjahan of Delhi built Tajmahal as a tomb for his wife in Agra. Architecturally, it is still one of the most beautiful buildings in the world. The building is made of fine white marble with inlays of coloured marble. It has open sides and many open arches. It rests on a platform or terrace of red sandstone. Four slender white towers rise from the corners of the terrace. There is a large dome above the central of the building. Around this large dome there are four smaller domes. Just inside the outer walls there is an open corridor from which visitors can look through carved marble screens into a central room. The bodies of Shahjahan and his wife Mumtaz lie in two graves below this room. The Tajmahal is surrounded by a beautiful garden and there is a beautiful pool that stretches out in front of the building. One can see the beauty of the Tajmahal on its reflection in the pool water. Visitors come to see this wonderful building at different times of the day since it assumes a different look at different times. Most people like it best on moonlit nights."

Questions:
(i) Why the Tajmahal was built?
(ii) Who is the mastermind behind this beautiful creation?
(iii) What does the building stand on?
(iv) Where are the two graves of Shahjahan and his wife situated?
(v) When does the Tajmahal take the most elegant look?

সারাংশ লিখুন:
আমার বিশ্বাস, শিক্ষা কেউ কাউকে দিতে পারে না। সুশিক্ষিত লোক মাত্রই স্বশিক্ষিত। আজকের বাজারে বিদ্যাদাতার অভাব নাই। এমন কি, এ ক্ষেত্রে দাতা কর্ণেরও অভাব নেই; এবং আমরা আমাদের ছেলেদের তাদের দ্বারস্থ করেই নিশ্চিন্ত থাকি এই বিশ্বাসে যে, সেখান থেকে তারা একটা বিদ্যার ধন লাভ করে ফিরে আসবে যার সুদে তার বাকি জীবন আরামে কাটিয়ে দিতে পারবে। কিন্তু, এ বিশ্বাস নিতান্ত অমূলক। মনোরাজ্যেও দান গ্রহণ সাপেক্ষ, অথচ আমরা দাতার মুখ চেয়ে গ্রহীতার কথাটা একেবারেই ভুলে যাই। এ সত্য ভুলে না গেলে আমরা বুঝতাম যে, শিক্ষকের সার্থকতা শিক্ষা দান করার নয়, কিন্তু ছাত্রকে তা অর্জন করতে সক্ষম করায়।

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
People moan about poverty as a great evil and it seems to be an accepted belief that people would be happy and more out of life if they had plenty of money. However there is more genuine satisfaction in life and more retained from life in the humble cottage of the poor than in the palace of the rich. I always pity the sons and daughters of the rich, who are attended by servants. It is because I know how sweet and pure the home of honest poverty is, how free its inmates are from envies and jealousies and how they are loving and united in the common interest of supporting the family. It is for these reasons that from the ranks of the poor so many young eminent self reliant men have always sprung and will spring.
It seems to be a matter of universal desire that poverty should be abolished. However, to abolish honest, industrious and self-denying poverty would be to destroy the soil upon which mankind produces the virtues that will enable our race to reach a still higher civilization than it now possesses.

Questions:
a) What do people generally think about poverty?
b) What is the author's opinion about it?
c) Why according to the author do eminent persons come from a poor family?
d) What will happen if poverty is abolished?
e) What will be suitable title for this passage?

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the questions below:
The true aim of education is the harmonious development of body, mind and soul. But mere bookish knowledge is not enough. Without co-curricular activities the full blooming of body, mind and soul is quite impossible. Co-curricular activities include debate, writing, cultural activities such as singing and dancing, sports and so on. The fact is that co-curricular activities are essential for the full development of the talents of the students. They provide ample opportunity for developing their faculties. Again games and sports are part and parcel of education because without a sound health a student cannot concentrate of his study. We all know the fact that health is wealth. Games and sports pave the way for building sound health. Moreover, co-curricular activities help the students to foster good will. They teach students to be polite, modest, gentle, loyal, diligent and perseverant. They also tighten the bonds of friendship and brotherhood among the students.

Questions:
i) What is the true aim of education?
ii) Why are co-curricular activities important?
iii) What are the common co-curricular activities?
iv) How do co-curricular activities help us?
v) How can games and sports contribute to proper education?

Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow: The greenhouse effect is not a new phenomenon. Scientists have known for centuries that a layer of gas naturally surrounds the earth like an insulating blanket, trapping the reflected energy of the sun and preventing it from escaping into space. This is what makes the earth warm enough for people, plants and animals. However, recent human activity has boosted the concentration of greenhouse gases and enhanced their heat trapping ability. The main culprit is Carbondioxide which scientist accounts for nearly half of global warming. CO2 is released from burning fossil fuels and from clearing and burning forests. CFCs may be accountable for 25% of global warming, but CO2 is the pivotal one. The most sophisticated computerized models of the USA and Britain agree that weather around the world will become more erratic and more extreme. In general, the temperature will rise more towards the pole that at the equator. Overall rainfall will also increase as higher temperatures boost evaporation from the seas. But the distribution of rain will shift. Some areas will become wetter, others will be drier. Global warming will also cause ocean levels to rise though not, as popular wisdom has it, due to the Antarctic ice cap melting. People living in low lying coastal region from New York and London to Jakarta and Dhaka will be in danger. Thunberg was known for changing how some people think and act about climate change. When she was only eight, she started learning about climate change. The more she learned, the more she was astonished as to why so little was being done about it. At the age of 11, Greta became so sad about climate change that she temporarily stopped speaking. She developed Asperger Syndrome, that affects the human faculty of socialization. Greta viewed her condition as positive and considered it as her "super power". She says it helped her see the world in black and white. In August 2018, Greta decided to go for action. Instead of going to school, she made a large sign that read "School Strike for climate". With that sign she quietly sat down outside the Swedish parliament. Her aim was to attract the notice of parliamentarians and put pressure on their mind to stop global warming. Greta's strike was picked up by the Swedish media and her voice started to spread all around the globe. Being inspired by Greta, in March 2019, climate campaigners across the world came together to co-ordinate the first 'Global Strike' for climate. txt:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions:
"Although social security programmes have very positive effects in reducing poverty and inequality, there is criticism that such programmes make people dependent on benefits. It is often argued that social security may reduce the working spirit of people. The economists raise questions whether the huge spending in social security could have been better utilized for the economic development of a country. However, evidence shows that the social security is a very effective tool for accelerated poverty reduction and sustained economic growth. On the other hand, there is hardly any proof that social security creates any disincentives to work. Moreover, the government has some obligations for social security as it is recognized by the Universal Declaration of Human Rights of the UN. It declares that 'Everyone, as a member of society, has the right to social security through national effort and international co-operations....' (Article-22). Bangladesh is a party to this declaration and therefore has obligations to introduce social security programmes for the vulnerable population."

Questions:
a) What are the positive impacts of social security?
b) What are the negative criticisms against social security?
c) Does social security make people reluctant to work?
d) What are the provisions of Universal Declaration of Human Rights regarding social security?
e) Why is the government of Bangladesh obliged to implement social security programmes?

txt:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions:
"Tension is so common a term but so difficult to define. It means strain or excitement or condition when feelings are tense, when relations between persons, groups, states etc. are strained. As regards an individual's tension, it saps his energy, destroys his power of imagination, deadens his sensibility and creativity, and eats into the vitals of life. No medicine has yet been invented to cure this disease, as it is no disease at all, yet it is the greatest one. It springs from many a factor from the unfulfillment of desire and from the frustration in life. A man of gigantic figure, tremendous physical strength, endless wealth and vast knowledge can be a victim of tension, but it never meets a man who has indomitable courage, strong will-force, unyielding spirit and who can think man is born to brave the thorns of life and sweet are the uses of adversity. He can smile away griefs, shake off anxieties, always take positive steps, welcome sorrows and sufferings and bear the brunt of life with fortitude and forbearance, calm and composure, prudence and sagacity. Hence, the man who harbours an optimistic attitude to life cherishes hopes and aspirations even in the midst of a sea of troubles, and nourishes steadfastness and singleness of sprint and purpose never yields to tension."

Questions:
a) Define tension according to the passage.
b) What is the effect of tension on an individual?
c) From which kind of individual does tension distance itself?

txt:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions:
"Social values are the custom, belief, taste, social practice, norms and attitude of a particular social community. Social values refer to the attitude or 'code of conduct' that an individual in certain society has to conform to. Social values determine course of social life of a person and regulate his or her life to a great extent. In the past, social values were very compact and rigid where every individual tried to maintain those values. But now people are sometimes callous or unconscious to social values. Lust, greed, injustice and discrimination are the causes of present degradation of social values. Consequently, we observe degradation of social values in our society. We see around us that youngsters do not show respect to their superiors, family ties break down, children go astray and young people get involved in various anti-social or immoral activities. We can develop intra-social relationship among its members, keep an eye on our youngsters and resist any such things to happen that destroy people's morality."

Questions:
a) What is social value?
b) What does social value refer to?
c) How do social values influence an individual?
d) Why are social values being degraded now-a-days?
e) What can be done to build a value-based society?

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the question that below:
Advertising has become a very specialized activity in modern times. In the business world of today, supply is usually greater than demand. There is great competition between different manufacturers of the same kind of product to persuade customers to buy their own particular brand. They always have to remind the customers of the names and the qualities of their products. They do this by advertising. The manufacturer advertises in the newspapers and posters. He sometimes pays for songs about his product in commercial radio programs. He employs attractive sales-girls to distribute samples of it. He organizes competitions, with prizes for the winners. He often advertises on the screens of local cinemas, most important of all, in countries that have television that will accept them. Manufacturers often spend large sums of money on advertisements. We buy a particular product because we think that it is the best. We usually think so because of the advertisements that say so. Some people never pause to ask themselves if the advertisements are telling the truth.

Questions:
a) Mention the kinds of advertisements you find in the passage.
b) Why do manufacturers spend so much money on advertising?
c) What do sales-girls do?
d) Do you think that we buy goods because they are advertised?
e) What is the thing some people do attracted by the advertisements?

Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
We, who live in the present day world, are proud to call ourselves civilized. Is it because we live and dress better than our forefathers? Of course, we have the advantages of the inventions of science which our ancestors had never known. But let us search our heart and ask ourselves, "Had science solved our problems?" Frankly speaking the answer is "no". In fact, science has added to our worries. Perhaps, now, we can kill more easily and swiftly than ever before. And then we have not given up the old habit of fighting. That is why we have wars after every decade or two. If we wish to be really civilized, let us learn to live in peace. Let us achieve the brotherhood of man.

a) Why do we feel proud in the present-day world?

ইংরেজি Reading Comprehension

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions below in your words:
"To be good is noble, but to teach others how to be good is nobler - and no trouble" said a well-known writer. This may explain why in this world there is more of preaching than of practice. We do not mean the preaching which are get in church, but that which is given freely and without stint, on buses, in the streets and even in the homes of our land. Where is the parent who does not discover himself telling his child to do just what he himself does regularly? How many people are there who are certain that they have never made anything but financial mistakes? The man who never swam a stroke feels perfectly competent to tell another how to swim. The man who cannot find his way to modest livelihood pretends to know just how to save the nation from all economic ills. It is not trouble to preach. But it is a considerable trouble to carry out what we preach. This is so true that the honest preacher preaches to himself even more then to his hearers every season. Only the man who is striving to climb the loftiest heights know just how difficult is the way.

Questions:
a) What does the quoted expression mean?
b) Why is practicing more difficult than preaching?
c) What does the writer mean by preaching?
d) What do the parents tell their children to do?
e) How does the honest preacher preach to himself?

ইংরেজি Reading Comprehension

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions:
Although classical dances like kathak, Bharatnatyam, Kathakali, Odissi and Manipuri are performed all over Bangladesh and India, those are traditionally associated with particular styles received from different regional schools. However, Bengal had no particular dance style of its own. Bengali artists learnt classical dancing in the past from teachers coming from South India, Madhya Pradesh and Manipur School of dances. Rabindranath Tagore played a major role in reviving Indian classical dance and creating a positive attitude towards it. He invited exponents of different classical dance forms to Shantiniketan and by merging various forms, Developed a new genre of Indian classical dance which came to be known as Rabindranritya or Tagore dance. Subsequently, Uday Shankar also helped to revive Indian dance but in a form closer to ballet than Rabindranritya which incorporates both dance and drama. Uday Shankar founded an institution at Almora in northern India and succeeded in popularising Indian classical dance nationally and internationally.

Questions:
a) What classical dances are generally performed in Bangladesh and India?
b) Who taught classical dancing to Bengali artists in the past?
c) What was Rabindranath Tagore's contribution to Indian classical dance?
d) What is Rabindranritya?
e) What is the difference between Rabindranritya and the style of classical dance created by Uday Shankar?

ইংরেজি Reading Comprehension

Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
Science and technology have come to pervade every aspect of our lives, and as a result, society is changing at a speed which is quite unprecedented. There is a great technological explosion around us penetrated by science. This explosion is already freeing vast number of people from their traditional bondage to nature, and now at last we have it is our power to free mankind once and for all from the fear which is based on want. Now, for the first time man can reasonably begin to think that life can be something more than a grim struggle for survival. But even today, in spite of the high standard of living which has become general in the more fortunate west, the majority of people in the world still spend nearly all their time and energy in a never-ending struggle with nature to secure the food and shelter they need.

Questions:
a) What pervades every aspect of our lives?
b) What explosion has science generated around us?
c) What has man in his power?
d) How is life in the west?
e) Who are engaged in a never-ending struggle with nature?

Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:
Try to imagine life without paper. Even in the era of emails and digital books, paper is all around us. We use paper not only for writing or printing, we use it in so many other ways every day. Light, strong and cheap, paper is in shopping bags, money, store receipts, cereal boxes and toilet tissues. So, where did this marvelously versatile material come from? According to ancient Chinese historical sources, a Chinese courtier named Ts'ai Lun invented paper in 105 AD as a substitute for silk and presented it to the emperor Hedi of the eastern Han Dynasty. But archaeological findings from Western China and Tibet suggest that paper was invented centuries earlier. Of course, people in various places around the world were writing long before the invention of paper. Materials such as bark, silk, wood and leather functioned in a similar way to paper. However, writing (and later printing) required a material that was both cheap and light weight to become truly ubiquitous.

Questions:
a) Why do we still find paper so useful in this era of emails and digital books?
b) Why is paper called a 'marvelously versatile material'?
c) Who is usually credited with inventing paper?
d) What makes us believe that paper was invented long before 105 AD?
e) What kind of materials did people use for writing before the invention of paper?

The secret of success in life lies in the proper use of time. Many of us are apt to forget that every moment is precious. Life is short and time is uncertain. During this limited and uncertain period, we have a lot of things to do. If we waste the precious minutes of our life in idleness, we will suffer and success will be difficult to achieve. It is only by utilizing every minute that we can hope to achieve success. Time once lost is lost forever. The young man who is afraid of work and idles away his time, is sure to find himself in later years a burden to himself and to others. There are some people who say that they have no time for reading books. They really deceive themselves. If they are punctual and industrious, they will find time to do everything. The industrious man has, in fact, the greatest amount of leisure, because he does his work regularly without idling for the next day.

While eating food, we should bear in mind that we do not eat just to satisfy hunger or to fill the belly. We eat to preserve our health. For good health we need good food. Sometimes it so happens that people who live even in the midst of plenty do not eat the food they need for good health, because they have no knowledge of the science of health and nutrition. They do not know how to select a balanced diet from many foods those are available to them. One of the main reasons of malnutrition in Bangladesh is our lack of knowledge of nutrition. Again, the poor and illiterate people in our country generally think that good and nutritive food means a costly food. They do not know that whatever food they get, could be good and nutritive if they could select the food items wisely to make it a balanced diet.

"আজকের দুনিয়াটা আশ্চর্যভাবে অর্থের বা বিত্তের ওপর নির্ভরশীল। লাভ ও লোভের দুর্নিবার গতি কেবল। আগে যাবার নেশায় লক্ষ্যহীন প্রচণ্ড বেগে শুধুই বিনাশের পথে এগিয়ে চলেছে। মানুষ যদি এ মূঢ়তাকে জয় না করতে পারে, তবে মনুষ্যত্ব কথাটাই হয়তো লোপ পেয়ে যাবে। মানুষের জীবন আজ এমন এক পর্যায়ে এসে পৌঁছেছে সেখান থেকে আর হয়তো নামবার উপায় নেই, এবার উঠবার সিঁড়ি না খুঁজলেই নয়।"

txt:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions below:
"Is it possible to persuade mankind to live without war? War is an ancient institution, which has existed for at least six thousand years. It was always wicked and usually foolish, but in the past the human race managed to live with it. Modern ingenuity has changed this. Either Man will abolish war, or war will abolish Man. For the present it is nuclear weapons that cause the greatest danger, but bacteriological or chemical weapons may, before long offer and even greater threat. If we succeed in abolishing nuclear weapons, our work will not be done until we have succeeded in abolishing war. To do this, we need to persuade mankind to look upon international questions in a new way, not as contests of force, in which the victory goes to the side which is most skillful in massacre, but by arbitration in accordance with agreed principles of law. It is not easy to change the age-old mental habits, but this is what must be attempted."

Questions:
a) How far can you date back the existence of war in the world?
b) What was the attitude of human race toward war in the past?
c) What should we do about war to make this world livable?
d) Do you find any ideological problem regarding war?
e) What do you suggest to put an end to war?

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
"I am convinced that inculcating of discipline at home and in the educational institutions is essential for the growth of every individual. It is however unfortunate that the needs for discipline in the youth is not sufficiently appreciated in this country. People seem to believe that to insist on discipline in the youth is not discipline is to be kind to the young. For me, what is unkind is to let a young person indulge in whatever s/he wants to do without parental, educational and ethical guidance. Discipline does not mean illogical harshness or oppressive imposition of law. Discipline involves ethics that is, i.e. responsible concern for the well-being of oneself and the other. Discipline involves guidance from the outside and control from the inside (self-control). Lack of guidance and control may lead a young person to waste her/his strength because s/he is yet to experience things in full. I feel sad when I see our youth-often individuals of talent, spirit and imagination-talking, behaving and acting as if they are their own judge and have the vision of predicting the future. I consider it as a wrong trend because it is detrimental to the physical, mental and social well-being of theirs and others as well."

Questions:
a) At what points do the author's and people's beliefs are different?
b) How does the author perceive discipline?
c) What according to the author, may befall when a youth lacks discipline?
d) What do you think is the dominant tone of the passage-prescriptive of dialogic? Engaging or distant? Why do you think so?
e) Write in brief your response to the author's take on discipline.

Read the passage and answer the following questions:
"Climate change refers to long term shifts in global weather patterns, primarily caused by human activities like fossil fuels, deforestation and industrial pollution. These activities release greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide and methane which trap heat in earth's atmosphere, leading to global warming. The effects of global warming are widespread and alarming. Rising temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt, leading to rising of sea levels, increasing threats to lives and nature. Extreme weather events, such a hurricane, droughts, floods and many other natural calamities are more frequent and severe, threatening agriculture, water sources and human settlements, especially in the vulnerable regions. To combat climate change, governments, organizations and individual must take action. Strategies include reducing green house gas emissions, switching to renewable energy sources like solar and wing and planting trees to absorb carbon dioxide. The 'Paris Agreement' aims to limit and integrate all efforts in the fight global warming."

"While eating food, we should bear in mind that we do not eat just to satisfy hunger or to fill the belly. We eat to preserve our health. For good health we need good food. Sometimes it so happens that people who live even in the midst of plenty do not eat the food they need for good health, because they have no knowledge of the science of health and nutrition. They do not know how to select at balanced diet from the many foods that are available to them. One of the main reasons of malnutrition in Bangladesh is our lack of knowledge of nutrition. Again, the poor and illiterate people in our country generally think that good and nutritive food means a costly food. They do not know that whatever food they get could be good and nutritive if they could select the food items wisely to make it a balanced diet."

English Comprehension English

Read the passage and answer the following questions:
"Florence Nightingale did not like easy and pleasant occupations of society; instead of going out to parties she visited London hospital and studied how sick people were nursed back to health and strength. She was shocked by the roughness and stupidity in those hospitals. She went out to Germany and France and learned there all she could about nursing. She returned to England and devoted herself to the hard task of improving the hospitals. Just then the Crimean War broke out. English soldiers went out singing to their death. But dreadful stories came home of wounded men being left to die. Everybody felt that something heroic must be done to put a stop to the sufferings of the brave soldiers. That was done by Florence Nightingale. She went to Crimea with about forty nurses and in a few months she brought order and comfort into what had been utter chaos and unspeakable misery."

Questions:
(a) Why did Florence Nightingale visit London hospitals?
(b) What shocked her in those hospitals?
(c) Why did she go to Germany and France?
(d) What did she do after returning to England?
(e) What did she do in Crimea?

txt:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
"Tension is so common a term but so difficult to define. It means strain or excitement of condition when feelings are tense, when relations between person, groups, states etc. are strained. As regards an individual's tension, it saps his energy, destroys his power of imagination, deadens his sensibility and creativity and eats into the vitals of life. No medicine has yet been invented to cure this disease, as it is no disease at all, yet it is the greatest one. It springs from many a factor; from the unfulfillment of desire and from the sheer frustration of life. A man of gigantic figure, tremendous physical strength, endless wealth and vast knowledge can be a victim of tension, but it never meets a man who has indomitable courage, strong will-force, unyielding spirit and who can think man is born to brave the thorns of life and sweet are uses of adversity. Hence, the man who harbours optimistic attitude of life, cherishes hopes and aspirations even in the midst of a sea of troubles, and nourishes steadfastness and singleness of spirit and purpose never yields to tension. And as regards tension between persons, groups or states, it can be overcome when the problems creating this condition are freely discussed."

Questions:
(a) How is tension defined?
(b) What does tension do to an individual?
(c) Who can be free from tension?
(d) Where does tension spring from?
(e) What should be done by persons, groups, or states for overcoming tension?

"The present age is called the age of information and mass media is the most effective instrument of sharing information. With the availability of technology and communication tools, the role and influence of mass media have become inextricable. In fact, they have very conspicuous impact on every aspect of our lives, our knowledge, our culture, our life style, policy making and many more. But what we need to know is that what is provided us with as being the sources of knowledge is not always innocent presentations. When the European colonized Africa, they called it a dark continent. They levelled it as the land of barbarous people. But actually, they are the people who invaded other people's land, exploited them and inflicted all inhuman tortures. The colonial authority looted those colonized lands and enriched themselves by making those lands barren. But nowhere in texts the European authors or the internalized native writers brought the realities into light. Even in present days, what information we get are not free from fabrications. In all respects, it is upon us to benefit or harm from media, to evaluate and judge the messages."

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
"The Bay of Bengal is widely considered a pivotal future for us. It is full of natural resources — both living and non-living. Living resources include a large variety of fish, animals, plants and weeds etc. Non-living resources are oil and gas, sands and minerals lying in and beneath the seabed. With technology, know-how and collaboration we can exploit these resources and contribute to the national economy. In the process, we can make significant progress in solving our unemployment problem. It is now easier and safer for us to harness these resources because we have successfully settled the maritime issues with our neighbors Myanmar and India. We can now attract foreign investment and collaboration in promoting our Blue Economy. We have both our territorial sea and the Exclusive Economic Zones to explore and exploit."

Questions:
a) Mention names of non-living resources in the Bay of Bengal both from the passage and from your knowledge.
b) What are the requirements to explore and exploit the natural resources in the Bay of Bengal?
c) Why is it easier now to extract our sea resources?
d) In what areas of the Bay of Bengal we can work, explore and extract the resources?

সারমর্ম লিখুনঃ
আমার একার সুখ, সুখ নহে ভাই,
সকলের সুখ, সখা, সুখ শুধু তাই।
আমার একার আলো সে যে অন্ধকার,
যদি না সবারে অংশ আমি দিতে পাই।
সকলের সাথে বন্ধু সকলের সাথে,
যাইব কাহারে বলো ফেলিয়া পশ্চাতে?
ভাইটি আমার সে তো ভাইটি আমার।
নিয়ে যদি নাহি পারি হতে অগ্রসর,
সে আমার দুর্বলতা, শক্তি সে তো নয়।
সবই আপন হেথা, কে আমার পর?
হৃদয়ের যোগ সে কি কভু ছিন্ন হয়?
এক সাথে বাঁচি আর এক সাথে মরি
এসো বন্ধু, এ জীবন মধুময় করি।

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the questions in your own words:
"Moral values are the foundation of a good character and a peaceful society. They guide people to distinguish between right and wrong and help them act responsibly. Qualities such as honesty, kindness, tolerance, and respect for others make a person morally strong. In recent times, society has witnessed a decline in moral values. Greed, dishonesty, and intolerance are increasing day by day. Many people ignore moral principles in the race for wealth and power. As a result, social harmony is disturbed and crimes are increasing. Moral values are first learned at home and later developed through education and social interaction. Without moral values, knowledge and intelligence may be misused. A nation where people lack moral values cannot ensure justice, harmony or long-term development. Therefore moral values are essential for both individual success and national progress."

Questions:
i) What are moral values compared to in the passage?
ii) What do moral values guide people to do?
iii) Name four moral qualities mentioned in the passage.
iv) What are the results of ignoring moral principles?
v) Why are moral values essential for a nation?

However, success is a relative phenomenon. Most people do not measure success by the virtue of honesty. They, like the character Dr. Faustus, are ready to sell their souls to the devil for immediate material success. But history shows that the individuals who upheld honesty even in adversity are remembered with love and admiration. Everybody should remember the proverb. "Honesty is the best policy."

A great part of Arabia is desert, where nothing but sand rock can be found. The sand is so hot that you cannot walk over it with your bare feet in daytime. Here and there in the desert, springs of water flow up from far beneath the ground, too deep for the sun to dry up. These springs are few and far apart, but wherever there is one, trees grow tall and graceful, making a cool, green, shady place around the spring; Such a place is called an oasis.
The Arabs who are not in the cities stay in the desert all year round. They live in tents that can be put up and taken down easily and quickly, allowing them to move from one oasis to another, in search for grass and water for their sheep, goats, camels and horses. These desert Arabs eat ripe sweet figs, as well as dates that grow on palm trees. They also dry the dates, and use them as food throughout the year.

txt:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:

"I am convinced that inculcating of discipline at home and in the educational institutions is essential for the growth of every individual. It is however unfortunate that the needs for discipline in the youth is not sufficiently appreciated in this country. People seem to believe that to insist on discipline in the youth is to be unkind to the young. I have a different opinion. For me, what is unkind is to let a young person indulge in whatever s/he wants to do without parental, educational and ethical guidance. Discipline does not mean illogical harshness or oppressive imposition of law. Discipline involves ethics that is, i.e. responsible concern for the well-being of oneself and the other. Discipline involves guidance from the outside and control from the inside (self-control). Lack of guidance and control may lead a young person to waste her/his strength because s/he is yet to experience things in full. I feel sad when I see our youth-often individuals of talent, spirit and imagination-talking, behaving and acting as if they are their own judge and have the vision of predicting the future. I consider it as a wrong trend because it is detrimental to the physical, mental and social well-being of theirs and others as well."

Questions:
a) At what points do the author's and people's beliefs differ?
b) How does the author perceive discipline?
c) What according to the author, may befall when a youth lacks discipline?
d) What do you think is the dominant tone of the passage—prescriptive or dialogic? Engaging or distant? Why do you think so?
e) Write in brief your response to the author's take on discipline.

"করোনা মহামারি শুরু হওয়ার আগে বিভিন্ন আন্তর্জাতিক সংস্থা দক্ষিণ এশিয়ার দেশগুলোকে অর্থনৈতিক প্রবৃদ্ধিতে চ্যাম্পিয়ন হিসেবে উল্লেখ করেছিল। কিন্তু মহামারির মাঝামাঝি এসে তারাই আবার বলছে, চলতি বছর এই অঞ্চল অর্থনীতিতে সবচেয়ে খারাপ করবে। বাংলাদেশসহ দক্ষিণ এশিয়ার দেশগুলো দারিদ্র্য বিমোচন এবং অন্যান্য খাতে উন্নয়নের দিকে সাফল্যের সাথে এগিয়ে যাচ্ছিল। কিন্তু করোনা মহামারির কারণে ঠিক উল্টোটাই ঘটেছে। সদ্য প্রকাশিত জাতিসংঘের বিশ্ব অর্থনৈতিক অবস্থার প্রতিবেদনে বলা হয়েছে, অর্থনীতি যে অবস্থায় পতিত হয়েছে তা থেকে উত্তরণে দেশগুলোকে দীর্ঘ পথ পাড়ি দিতে হবে। তবে এতো কিছুর পরও বাংলাদেশের রেমিট্যান্স প্রবাহ অব্যাহত আছে এবং আমাদের বৈদেশিক মুদ্রার রিজার্ভের পরিমাণ রেকর্ড পরিমাণ ছাড়িয়েছে।"

Solve the following mathematical problems:
(a) Train speed: A train is running at a speed of 40 km/hr and it crosses a post in 18 seconds. What is the length of the train?
(b) Work & Time: Kamal will complete a work in 18 days. If Shahin is 20% more efficient than Kamal, in how many days can he complete the work?
(c) Train Stoppage: A train travelled at an average speed of 100 km/hr, stopping for 3 minutes after every 75 km. How long did it take to reach its destination 600 km from the starting point?
(d) H.C.F & L.C.M: What is the smallest number by which 3,600 must be divided to make it a perfect cube?
(e) Algebra: If \(2^n = \sqrt{1024}\), what is the value of n?
(f) Equation: In an examination, a student scores 4 marks for every correct answer and loses 1 mark for every wrong answer. If he attempts all 80 questions and secures 120 marks, how many questions does he answer correctly?
(g) Compound Interest: A bank offers 5% compound interest calculated on half-yearly basis. A customer deposits Tk. 1,600 each on 1st January and 1st July of a year. At the end of the second year, how much interest will he receive?
(h) Percentage: A reduction of 10% in the price of a pen enabled a trader to purchase 9 more pens for Tk. 540. What is the reduced price of the pen?
(i) Circular Track / L.C.M: A, B and C start at the same time in the same direction to run around a circular stadium. A completes a round in 252 seconds, B in 308 seconds and C in 198 seconds. After what time will they meet again at the starting point?
(j) Logarithm: If \(\log_5(x^2 + x) - \log_5(x + 1) = 3\), find the value of x.

"Today marks the 49 years of our existence as a sovereign nation. On this day in 1971, our struggle for independence following a nine-month war was rewarded with a richly deserved victory that came at the cost of unimaginable loss of life and persecution. We should always remember with a deep sense of gratitude, the enormous contributions of the freedom fighters who fought and bled on the ground and the leading role of Bangabandhu and his four trusted lieutenants in steering us to this moment. Together, their efforts and sacrifices, as well as that of countless other individuals both at home and abroad, paved the way for the fulfilment of the Bengali dream for self-determination."
